name: adjustTableFormat
specification:
Functional Description: Adjusts the formatting of a given TableDefinition by recalculating the maximum and minimum widths of each column based on the headers and cell contents. It ensures that the total width of the table does not exceed the maximum allowed width, rescaling the widths of scalable columns if necessary, and returns a new TableDefinition with the adjusted styles.

Args:
table: TableDefinition - The TableDefinition object containing headers, rows, and text styles to be adjusted

Returns: TableDefinition - A new TableDefinition object with updated text styles reflecting the adjusted column widths

Preconditions:
1. The input TableDefinition must not be null
2. The TableDefinition must contain at least one header and corresponding rows
3. Each TextStyle in the table must be properly initialized with valid max and min width values

Postconditions:
1. A new TableDefinition is returned with updated text styles
2. The original TableDefinition remains unchanged
3. The adjusted styles account for header lengths and cell contents

Invariants:
1. The maximum width of each column is always at least as large as the length of the corresponding header
2. The total width of the table does not exceed the maximum allowed width after adjustments
3. Scalable columns are resized proportionally if the total calculated width exceeds the adjusted maximum width

Exception:
IllegalArgumentException - If the input TableDefinition is invalid (e.g., contains null headers or rows)

name: addOptionGroup
specification:
Functional Description: Adds an OptionGroup to the Options instance, managing its required status and the options it contains. If the OptionGroup is required, it is added to the list of required options, and each option within the group is set to not required, ensuring that no individual option can be required if it belongs to a required group.

Args:
optionGroup: OptionGroup - The OptionGroup instance to be added, which contains multiple options and may have a required status

Returns: Options - The current Options instance, allowing for method chaining

Preconditions:
1. The optionGroup parameter must not be null
2. The OptionGroup must be properly initialized with options before being passed to this method
3. The Options instance must be in a valid state to accept new option groups

Postconditions:
1. The OptionGroup is added to the Options instance, affecting the internal state of required options
2. Each option within the OptionGroup is added to the Options instance and marked as not required
3. The internal mapping of option keys to their respective OptionGroup is updated

Invariants:
1. An Option cannot be required if it is part of an OptionGroup
2. The requiredOpts list is updated to reflect the addition of the OptionGroup if it is required
3. The optionGroups map maintains a consistent relationship between option keys and their associated OptionGroup

Exception:
None

name: indexOfWrap
specification:
Functional Description: Determines the index of a character in a given CharSequence that can be used as a line break, based on a specified width and starting position. It first checks for any break characters within the specified width, and if none are found, it looks for the last whitespace character before the limit; if no whitespace is found, it returns the limit minus one.

Args:
text: CharSequence - The text in which to search for a line break character
width: int - The maximum number of characters to consider for a line break; must be greater than 0
startPos: int - The starting position in the text from which to begin searching for a line break

Returns: int - The index of the found break character or the limit minus one if no suitable break character is found

Preconditions:
1. width must be greater than 0
2. startPos must be a valid index within the bounds of the text
3. text must not be null

Postconditions:
1. Returns a valid index within the bounds of the text
2. Input parameters remain unchanged
3. The method does not modify the text or any external state

Invariants:
1. The method always returns an index that is either a break character position or a calculated limit
2. If width is greater than the length of the text, the method will handle it gracefully
3. The search for break characters is performed in a defined order (first within width, then last whitespace)

Exception:
IllegalArgumentException - If width is less than 1
